frames.narration: A team has 40 points of work per sprint and code with 30 points of debt. In hot code, changed every sprint, a feature costs 10 points plus 1 for every 10 points of debt: 13 now. Each rushed feature adds 2 points of debt.

Option one: ignore it. Debt compounds: after 24 sprints it is 120 and one feature costs 22 points. The team has delivered 45 features, and each one is slower than the last. That slowdown is the interest.

Option two: spend 8 points of each sprint on small refactoring steps, with tests. Each step removes 6 points of debt. After 24 sprints debt is 14, a feature costs 11, and the team has delivered 64 features. It pulls ahead of option one from sprint 11.

Same plan without tests. Every third sprint a refactoring step changes behaviour by accident, and a regression costs 12 points to find and fix: 8 regressions in 24 sprints. It still delivers 57 features, but it only pulls ahead from sprint 14.

Option three: stop and rewrite for 6 sprints. Nothing is delivered for 6 sprints, the new code collects rushed-feature debt as soon as it ships, and after 24 sprints the team has 42 features: still behind the team that ignored the debt, which only gets passed at sprint 28.

Now the debt is in cold code that nobody changes. A feature always costs 10 points. Ignoring the debt delivers 96 features in 24 sprints, repaying it in small steps delivers 72, and a rewrite also 72. Here the best plan is to leave it alone.

Repay where the interest is: hot code, in small, tested steps, as a steady share of every sprint. Write deliberate shortcuts down. Leave stable, untouched code alone, and be wary of any rewrite that stops delivery.
